title: AsyncSequence and AsyncStream
summary: An `AsyncSequence` is a list of values that arrive over time, read with `for await`. `AsyncStream` turns callback- or delegate-based sources into one.
body: **In simple words:** A normal array has all values now. An async sequence gives values one by one as they arrive: lines of a file, WebSocket messages, location updates. You read them with `for await value in sequence { }`.

**AsyncStream:** the easy way to make your own. You get a `continuation`; call `yield(value)` when something arrives and `finish()` when done. Set `onTermination` to clean up (stop location updates, close sockets).

**Buffering:** if values arrive faster than you read them, they buffer. Choose a policy: `.bufferingNewest(1)` for "only latest matters" (location), `.unbounded` only when you are sure the producer is slow.
**One reader:** an `AsyncStream` should have one consumer. For many listeners, create one stream per listener (a broadcaster) or use Combine.
**Ending:** the loop ends when the stream finishes or the task is cancelled. Cancel the task (or let SwiftUI `.task` do it) to avoid endless loops holding `self`.
**Extras:** swift-async-algorithms adds `debounce`, `merge`, `combineLatest`, `chunked` for async sequences. `Observations` (Swift 6.2) turns `@Observable` changes into an async sequence.
keyPoints: Pull-based stream consumed with `for await`; works with cancellation.
Pick a buffering policy to avoid memory growth.
Prefer async sequences for new code; Combine still fine for rich operator pipelines.

code.caption: Wrapping location updates

mistakes: Using `.unbounded` with a fast producer and growing memory.
Starting `for await` in an unstructured `Task` that is never cancelled.
followups: **AsyncSequence vs Combine publisher?** Pull vs push; async sequences integrate with async/await and cancellation; Combine has more operators.
**How do you convert a Combine publisher?** `publisher.values` gives an async sequence.
